input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages (I think they’re called MMS?) from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

I see that my phone shows good signal strength and 5G with data enabled at the top. I can make regular calls and send normal text messages just fine. I’m not sure about browsing the internet when not on Wi-Fi, though—should I try that?
I turned off Wi-Fi like you said, but it looks like I can’t get on the internet using just my mobile data. Does that mean something’s wrong with my data connection? What should I do next?

Oh, I see. I definitely don’t want to change my plan, but I’m okay with adding more data if that will fix it. Could you please add 2GB for me? And just to double-check, it’ll be $4.00 for 2GB, right? I want to make sure I understand before you do anything.

Yes, please go ahead and add the 2GB for $4.00. Thank you for explaining it so clearly! What happens after you add it—will my picture messages start working right away, or do I need to do anything else?

It’s been a few minutes, but I still can’t send picture messages. Do I really have to restart my phone? I get nervous about losing my photos or something going wrong. Is there anything else I can try first?

I tried turning Airplane Mode on and off like you suggested, but I still can’t send picture messages. My mobile data shows as enabled at the top of my phone. Is there anything else I can do before restarting? I just get so anxious about restarting my phone.

I went ahead and reset the APN settings like you mentioned. It says the changes will take effect after I restart my phone. I’m still a bit nervous—are you sure restarting won’t mess up anything important, like my photos or contacts? I just want to be extra careful.
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working? Is there anything else we can try?

Wi-Fi Calling is turned off on my phone, and I can still send regular text messages just fine after the restart. When I try to send a picture message, it just keeps trying to send but never goes through—there’s no specific error message, it just spins. What should I do next?

I checked my messaging app’s permissions, and it looks like it only has permission for the phone. It doesn’t seem to have access to storage or SMS. Could that be why I can’t send picture messages? How do I fix this?

I’ve granted both the storage and SMS permissions to my messaging app. I just tried sending a picture message, and it finally worked! Thank you so much for your help and patience—I really appreciate it.

Thank you so much for your patience and reassurance along the way. I really appreciate your help—technology can be so overwhelming for me sometimes! I’ll reach out if I have any more trouble. Have a great day! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

It’s been a few minutes, but I still can’t send picture messages. Do I really have to restart my phone? I get nervous about losing my photos or something going wrong. Is there anything else I can try first?

Restarting your phone is a safe and common step that helps your device recognize the newly added data and refresh its network connection. You won’t lose any photos or personal data by restarting.

However, before you restart, we can try a few other steps:
1. Turn Airplane Mode ON for about 10 seconds, then turn it OFF.
2. Make sure mobile data is enabled in your phone’s settings.
3. Try sending a picture message again.

If these steps don’t work, a restart is the next best step and is very safe. Would you like to try these steps first, or would you like instructions on how to restart your phone?

Resetting APN settings is safe and won’t delete any of your personal data or photos. After resetting, you will need to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Rest assured, restarting your phone is completely safe and will not affect your photos, contacts, messages, or any other personal data. Restarting simply refreshes your phone’s system and network connections, which is necessary for the new APN settings to take effect.

It’s a standard troubleshooting step and is very commonly used to resolve issues like the one you’re experiencing. You won’t lose any information or settings by doing this.

I checked my messaging app’s permissions, and it looks like it only has permission for the phone. It doesn’t seem to have access to storage or SMS. Could that be why I can’t send picture messages? How do I fix this?

Yes, that is very likely the reason you can’t send picture messages. Your messaging app needs permission to access storage (to attach and send photos) and SMS (to send messages).

To fix this, you need to grant your messaging app both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions. Here’s how you can do it:

1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and select your messaging app.
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Enable both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions.

After granting these permissions, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue!
